artifacts.summary: Confirms the base-mode territory gap exactly (two independent gates: h1_territory population and hard-mode-only territory.md contract pull-in), locates the exact insertion points in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (probed_dispatch_post_h1 as the sibling set) and orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh (the existing ungated '## Territory' block), rules out reusing orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's admission jq for the payload, and recommends an explicit absent/coarse-scope sentinel coordinated with task 165 rather than duplicating its admission-posture ruling.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's /orchestrate multi-task engine, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's `probed_dispatch_post_h1` array (built after H1 refusals are filtered, before the live-dispatch loop) is the canonical 'concurrently-dispatched siblings this cycle' set -- already computed once, shared by dry-run and live paths. Any future feature needing 'who else is being dispatched right now' should read from this array rather than re-deriving it from orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's admit/defer verdicts, which only expose collision facts (not a full sibling roster) and are a deliberately separate admission-decision concern.

orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's file_scope collision gate uses an asymmetric in-batch tie-break: for two same-batch tasks whose file_scope overlaps, only the HIGHER task_number sees the collision (scope_kind == in_batch filtered by other_num < c) and is deferred; the lower-numbered one is admitted with zero signal about the collision or the colliding sibling. Also confirmed: file_scope // [] | length == 0 short-circuits to unconditional admit with no collision check at all -- an absent scope is invisible to this gate by construction, not by omission bug.
